extracted.intended_audience: Researchers applying to NIH grants who received a Summary Statement and are preparing a resubmission
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance for preparing an NIH grant resubmission after an unfunded initial submission, focusing on analyzing the Summary Statement, revising the application, and writing the required Introduction. Emphasizes prioritizing reviewer concerns and documenting responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission opportunity and deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: You have one opportunity to resubmit your proposal. The resubmission deadline is 37 months from the original submission date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of the single resubmission chance and the timing constraint when planning revisions and gathering additional data or input.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address reviewers' concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: Address all the reviewers' concerns and feedback in your resubmission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Your resubmission should explicitly respond to critiques in the Summary Statement; failure to address reviewer concerns will reduce the chance of funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analyze the Summary Statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Carefully read through the Summary Statement and identify the main concerns and suggestions from the reviewers. Categorize these into major and minor issues, and prioritize addressing the major issues first.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systematically categorize reviewer comments (major vs. minor) and create a prioritized plan to resolve the most important criticisms before attending to smaller edits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek external input on critiques
rubrics_metrics.description: Share the Summary Statement with colleagues, mentors, or a grant proposal writing instructor to gain additional perspectives on the feedback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use external reviewers to validate your interpretation of criticisms, suggest concrete fixes, and catch issues you may have missed; mentors can advise on strategic responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strengthen the scientific rationale and hypotheses
rubrics_metrics.description: Strengthen the scientific rationale and hypotheses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarify and bolster the underlying logic of the project and how hypotheses follow from preliminary evidence and literature; make the significance and novelty explicit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide additional preliminary data if needed
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide additional preliminary data, if needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If reviewers questioned feasibility or evidence, add new or reanalyzed data to support feasibility and the proposed hypotheses; use data to directly address specific critiques.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarify experimental design and methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarify the experimental design and methodology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resolve ambiguities by adding detail on experimental procedures, controls, analytic plans, and statistical approaches to demonstrate rigor and reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address budget and resource concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: Address any concerns about the budget or resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Justify costs, confirm availability of equipment and personnel, and revise the budget to align with the scope and reviewer expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Craft a concise Introduction summarizing changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Include an Introduction that summarizes the changes made in response to the reviewers' feedback. This should be concise and clearly demonstrate how you have addressed each concern.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly map reviewer comments to the revisions made in the application (comment → response → location in text); keep the introduction brief and focused on demonstrating that critiques were taken seriously and corrected.
